title: UK personal loans: how to apply and compare the real cost
summary: Compare written offers, understand representative APR and check early settlement before committing to monthly repayments.
content:
# UK personal loans: how to apply and compare the real cost

Last updated: 2026-11-27

## Know what you are putting at risk
An unsecured personal loan normally pays you a lump sum and you repay it over an agreed term, often in fixed monthly instalments. A secured loan puts an asset such as your home at risk if repayments fail. Unsecured borrowing can still have serious consequences if you miss payments. Set a budget that covers rent, bills and irregular expenses before deciding how much you can repay. [Borrowing types](#guide-evidence-types)

## From eligibility check to written offer
Check the lender’s age, residence, income and address rules. Use a confirmed soft-search checker first if available. Give accurate employment and income details and check your credit reports. A full application usually uses a hard search. A representative APR is an advertising figure: the rate or lower is expected for at least 51% of agreements arising from the promotion. It does not mean 51% of applicants get approved. Compare your own offer’s actual APR, amount received, fees, instalments, total payable and term on the same borrowing amount. [APR and application](#guide-evidence-apply) · [Credit history and searches](/en/money/uk-credit-history-and-credit-score)

## Worked example: two offers to borrow £3,000
Assume no upfront fee and equal monthly instalments. At £140 for 24 months, repay £3,360, or £360 above the amount borrowed. At £100 for 36 months, repay £3,600, or £600 above the amount borrowed. The second is £40 a month lower but costs £240 more overall. Ask for the actual figures in writing, including any fees, before accepting. [Comparing costs](#guide-evidence-example)

## Check early repayment and consolidation
On a regulated agreement you can generally repay early. Ask for a dated settlement figure, including any applicable interest or charges, and check separately how partial overpayments work. The displayed balance, settlement figure and sum of remaining instalments can differ. For consolidation, compare the total cost including closure fees, avoid borrowing again on cleared accounts, and check whether the new loan puts property at risk. Lower monthly payments can mean paying more over a longer term. [Early repayment](#guide-evidence-settlement)

## Watch for fraud and get support early
Be wary of guaranteed approval or an unexpected fee for releasing funds. Verify the firm and its phone number through the FCA rather than using details from the message. Never pay under pressure. If you cannot afford bills or debt repayments, contact your lender and get free independent debt advice before taking on more credit. General information only, without personalised financial advice. [Loan fee fraud](#guide-evidence-support) · [Free debt advice](#guide-evidence-debt) · [Bank accounts for newcomers](/en/money/open-uk-bank-account-new-arrival)
